description: Orchestration Loop panel — iterative develop-rebuild-verify loop for testing changes. Supports two modes: Simple (runs an existing workflow repeatedly with reflection-based exit) and Pipeline (builds workflows from description, runs them, optionally diagnoses via UI Bridge assertions, reflects, implements fixes, and rebuilds). Includes a saved config library with favorites, a multi-runner mode for parallel orchestration across runner instances, and an iteration history table with diagnostic result expansion.

groups.name: Page Structure & Layout
groups.description: The orchestration loop panel fills its container with a header bar and scrollable content area. The header contains the title, mode toggle, phase badge, iteration counter, and action buttons.

assertions.description: The panel heading 'Orchestration Loop' is visible in the header bar
A 'Multi' toggle button is present in the header to switch between single-runner and multi-runner modes
A 'Run Loop' button is visible when the loop is not running
A subtitle describing the panel's purpose is visible below the header: 'Iterative develop-rebuild-verify loop for testing changes to the runner itself.'
assertions.precondition: Loop is not running, single mode

groups.name: Saved Config Library
groups.description: Users can save, load, overwrite, favorite, and delete orchestration loop configurations. The library panel shows all saved configs with name, mode, and last updated date. Favorites appear as quick-load buttons below the header when the library is closed.

assertions.description: A 'Library' button is present in the header when the loop is not running, allowing users to open the saved configurations panel
A 'Save' button is present in the header when the loop is not running, allowing users to save the current form state as a named config

Clicking the Library button opens a panel titled 'Saved Configurations' showing a count of saved configs and a list of config entries. Each entry shows the config name, mode type, and last updated date. Each entry has hover-visible Save (overwrite) and Trash (delete) icons, and a Star toggle for favoriting.

When the library is closed and favorited configs exist, favorite config names appear as small quick-load buttons preceded by a yellow star icon. Clicking a quick-load button loads that config's form state into the form.
assertions.precondition: At least one config is favorited and library panel is closed

groups.name: Mode Selection — Simple vs Pipeline
groups.description: The config form provides two radio buttons to choose between Simple mode (runs an existing workflow by ID) and Pipeline mode (builds workflows from description, with optional fixes and diagnostics). Pipeline mode is the default.

assertions.description: A 'Simple' radio button option is available in the config form
A 'Pipeline' radio button option is available in the config form and is selected by default
In Simple mode, the form shows a Workflow text input and an Exit strategy dropdown with options: Reflection (0 fixes), Verification, Fixed Iterations, and Diagnostic Evaluation

groups.name: Common Controls — Between, Max, Target, Options
groups.description: Both modes share common controls for iteration behavior, maximum iteration count, target runner selection, and behavioral toggles (retry on failure, wait for fixer, use worktree).

assertions.description: A 'Between' dropdown controls what happens between iterations with options: Signal (rebuild), Signal (no rebuild), Always (rebuild), Always (no rebuild), Wait Healthy, None
A 'Max' number input sets the maximum iteration count (1-50), default value 5
A 'Target' dropdown selects which runner to target. Shows 'This runner (self)' as default, plus any managed runner instances with their name and port
A 'Retry on failure' checkbox is available with description '— Re-run after fixer completes'
A 'Run in isolated worktree' checkbox creates a new git branch and worktree for the run

groups.name: Pipeline Mode — Build, Fix, and Diagnose Configuration
groups.description: Pipeline mode displays textarea inputs for build description and context, optional fix context, and diagnostic phase configuration. The pipeline has three capability toggles: Enable Fix Implementation and Enable Diagnostic Phase.

assertions.description: A 'Build Description' textarea is present in pipeline mode for describing the workflow to generate
assertions.precondition: Pipeline mode is selected, loop not running

assertions.description: A 'Build Context (optional)' textarea is present for providing additional context to the builder
assertions.precondition: Pipeline mode is selected, loop not running

assertions.description: An 'Enable Fix Implementation' checkbox is present with description '— Spawns Claude Code after reflection'. When enabled, a third 'Fix Context (optional)' textarea column appears in the grid.
assertions.precondition: Pipeline mode is selected, loop not running

assertions.description: An 'Enable Diagnostic Phase' checkbox is present with description '— UI Bridge assertions after execution'. Enabling it reveals the diagnostic configuration panel and an exit strategy dropdown.
assertions.precondition: Pipeline mode is selected, loop not running

assertions.description: A 'Workflow (fallback)' text input allows specifying an existing workflow ID to use when build is not configured
assertions.precondition: Pipeline mode is selected, loop not running

groups.name: Diagnostic Configuration Panel
groups.description: When 'Enable Diagnostic Phase' is checked, a teal-bordered configuration panel appears with fields for UI Bridge assertions, DOM snapshot capture options, and an optional model override. An exit strategy dropdown also appears with Reflection, Diagnostic Evaluation, and Fixed Iterations options.

assertions.description: The diagnostic config panel has a teal-colored heading 'Diagnostic Configuration' and a teal border/background
A monospace textarea labeled 'Assertions (JSON array)' accepts a JSON array of UI Bridge assertion objects. The placeholder shows example assertions with 'type', 'role', 'name', 'min' fields.
A 'Capture DOM snapshot' checkbox is present and checked by default, controlling whether the diagnostician captures a DOM snapshot for AI triage
A 'Max chars' number input sets the maximum DOM snapshot character count (1000-50000, step 1000), defaulting to 8000

A 'Model override' text input allows specifying a specific AI model for diagnostic triage (e.g., 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514'), with '(default)' as placeholder text. When populated, the value is sent as diagnose.model_override in the pipeline config and the backend routes the triage AI call to that model instead of the default. When empty, the backend uses default model routing.

When diagnostics are enabled in pipeline mode, an 'Exit' strategy dropdown appears with options: Reflection (0 fixes), Diagnostic Evaluation, and Fixed Iterations. The Diagnostic Evaluation option exits the loop when all diagnostic assertions pass.
assertions.precondition: Enable Diagnostic Phase is checked, pipeline mode

assertions.description: Clicking 'Run Loop' with invalid JSON in the assertions textarea shows an error 'Diagnostic assertions contain invalid JSON' and does not start the loop. If the JSON is valid but not an array, it shows 'Diagnostic assertions must be a JSON array'.
assertions.precondition: Enable Diagnostic Phase is checked, invalid JSON in assertions textarea

groups.name: Running State — Progress, Phase, Controls
groups.description: When the loop is running, the config form hides and is replaced by a progress bar showing current phase, iteration progress, and action buttons (Stop, Signal).

assertions.description: While running, a progress bar shows the current iteration out of max iterations (e.g., '2/5') with a colored fill indicating progress percentage

A phase badge appears in the header and progress bar showing the current loop phase (e.g., 'running workflow', 'building workflow', 'diagnosing', 'reflecting', 'implementing fixes', 'waiting for fixer'). Each phase has a distinct color: blue for running_workflow, yellow for building_workflow, teal for diagnosing, purple for reflecting, orange for implementing_fixes, cyan for waiting_for_fixer, green for complete, red for error.
assertions.precondition: Loop is running or has completed

assertions.description: A red 'Stop' button appears in the header while the loop is running
A yellow 'Signal' button appears in the header while the loop is running AND the between-iterations mode is 'restart_on_signal'. Clicking it signals the loop to proceed to the next iteration.
assertions.precondition: Loop is running with restart_on_signal between mode

groups.name: Iteration History Table
groups.description: A table showing results for each completed iteration with columns: #, Duration, Exit, Reason, Diag, Pipeline. Each row summarizes one iteration's outcome.

assertions.description: The iteration history section has a heading 'Iteration History' with an iteration count (e.g., '3 iterations')
The table has 6 column headers: #, Duration, Exit, Reason, Diag, Pipeline
When no iterations have run, the table shows 'No iterations yet' centered across all columns

Each iteration row shows: iteration number (e.g., '#1'), duration in seconds (e.g., '12.3s'), exit status ('EXIT' in green or 'CONTINUE' in yellow), reason text (truncated with tooltip), and pipeline metadata (e.g., 'fixes=3, applied=yes, rebuild'). The iteration number column is primary-colored and semibold.
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration has completed

groups.name: Diagnostic Results Display
groups.description: The Diag column in the iteration history shows diagnostic evaluation results. When diagnostic data exists, the row is clickable with expand/collapse chevrons. The PASS/FAIL badge shows the result and root cause category. Expanding a row reveals diagnosis text, prompt rewrite suggestion, and individual assertion results.

assertions.description: When a diagnostic evaluation passed, the Diag column shows a green 'PASS' badge with green background tint
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration has a passing diagnostic result

assertions.description: When a diagnostic evaluation failed, the Diag column shows a red 'FAIL' badge followed by the root cause category (e.g., 'FAIL · bad ui rendering'). Root cause categories include: bad ui rendering, bad ui bridge evaluation, bad verification steps, bad generation prompt, bad state machine logic, infrastructure issue, unknown.
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration has a failing diagnostic result

assertions.description: Rows with diagnostic data show a right-pointing chevron (▶) before the iteration number. Clicking the row expands it to show a detail section, and the chevron rotates to point downward (▼). Clicking again collapses it.
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration has diagnostic data

assertions.description: The expanded diagnostic detail row shows the diagnosis text prefixed with 'Diagnosis:' in teal. If a prompt rewrite suggestion exists, it appears in a teal-bordered highlight box prefixed with 'Suggested prompt rewrite:'. If assertion results exist, they appear as small chips showing the assertion type with a checkmark (✓ green) or cross (✗ red) indicating pass/fail. Hovering an assertion chip shows the full JSON details as a tooltip.
When an iteration has no diagnostic result (diagnostics not configured or skipped), the Diag column shows '--' in muted text
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration without diagnostic data

groups.name: Diagnostic Phase — Pipeline Behavior
groups.description: The diagnostic phase runs between Execute and Reflect in the pipeline loop. It captures page health, runs UI Bridge assertions, and uses AI triage to classify failures. The phase is skipped when the workflow crashed. When diagnostics fail, the next iteration rebuilds the workflow with diagnostic context injected into the prompt.

assertions.description: When a workflow execution fails (status is not 'completed' or 'complete'), the diagnostic phase is skipped entirely and no diagnostic result appears in the iteration row's Diag column. This prevents misleading triage results from undefined page state after crashes.
assertions.precondition: An iteration completed where the workflow failed

assertions.description: When a diagnostic evaluation fails and the pipeline has a build configuration, the next iteration rebuilds the workflow with diagnostic context injected. The iteration row should show 'rebuild' in the Pipeline column after a failed diagnostic.
assertions.precondition: An iteration with failed diagnostic and build config enabled

assertions.description: With 'Diagnostic Evaluation' exit strategy selected, when a diagnostic evaluation passes (all assertions pass, page healthy), the loop exits. The final iteration row shows 'EXIT' in the Exit column with reason mentioning 'Diagnostic evaluation passed'.
assertions.precondition: Loop ran with diagnostic_evaluation exit strategy and diagnostics eventually passed

assertions.description: When a model override is configured in the diagnostic phase (e.g., 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514'), the triage AI call during the diagnosing phase routes to that specific model via run_prompt_with_model_override. When the model override field is empty or '(default)', the triage call uses the default model routing. This is verifiable by observing that diagnostic results are produced (the triage call succeeds) regardless of which model is specified, and the iteration row's Diag column shows a PASS or FAIL badge rather than an error state.
assertions.precondition: Loop ran with diagnostics enabled and a model_override value configured

assertions.description: During the diagnostic phase, the phase badge shows 'diagnosing' in teal color (text-teal-400 foreground, bg-teal-500/10 background), matching the diagnostic config panel's color scheme
assertions.precondition: Loop is running and in the diagnosing phase

groups.name: Visual Design & Typography
groups.description: The orchestration loop panel follows the runner's dark theme with consistent typography, spacing, and color usage. Form inputs use the shared inputCls style (muted background, bordered, rounded), and the panel uses a scrollbar-dark class for the content area.

assertions.description: All form inputs (text, number, select, textarea) use a consistent style: muted background (bg-muted), bordered (border-border), rounded corners, small text (text-xs), with focus ring on primary color
Form labels use a consistent style: small text (text-[0.78rem]) in muted foreground color (text-muted-foreground)

The diagnostic configuration panel uses teal-themed styling: border-teal-500/20 border, bg-teal-500/5 background, text-teal-400 heading. The prompt rewrite suggestion box in expanded results uses matching teal styling: border-teal-500/30 left border, bg-teal-500/5 background.
Error messages appear in a left-bordered container with red styling: border-red-500 left border, bg-red-500/10 background, text-red-400 text color

groups.name: Form State Save/Load Round-Trip
groups.description: All form fields including diagnostic configuration persist correctly through the save/load cycle. Saving a config captures the complete form state, and loading it restores all fields including diagnostic assertions, snapshot settings, and model override.

assertions.description: Saving the current form state as a named config and then loading it restores all fields: mode, workflowId, targetPort, targetRunnerId, supervisorPort, maxIter, exitStrategy, between, buildDesc, buildContext, enableFixes, fixContext, retryOnFailure, waitForFixer, useWorktree, enableDiagnose, diagnoseAssertions, diagnoseCaptureSnapshot, diagnoseSnapshotMaxChars, and diagnoseModelOverride. The loaded state should be identical to what was saved.
Overwriting an existing saved config updates its config_json and updated_at timestamp while preserving its id, name, and is_favorite status
assertions.precondition: Library panel is open with at least one saved config

states.name: Idle — Config Form Visible
states.description: No loop is running. The config form is displayed with mode selection (Simple/Pipeline), common controls (Between, Max, Target), behavioral checkboxes, and the Run Loop button. The header shows Library and Save buttons. Favorite quick-load buttons may appear below the header if any configs are favorited.

states.name: Configuring — Library Panel Open
states.description: The saved configurations library panel is open, showing a 'Saved Configurations' heading with a count and list of saved configs. Each entry shows name, mode, and last updated date. The config form remains visible behind the library panel. Users can load, overwrite, favorite, or delete configs.

transitions.name: Start the loop while library is open

states.name: Running — Loop Executing Iterations
states.description: The orchestration loop is actively executing. The config form is hidden and replaced by a progress bar showing iteration count (e.g., '2/5') and a colored fill. A phase badge in the header shows the current sub-phase: running workflow (blue), building workflow (yellow), diagnosing (teal), reflecting (purple), implementing fixes (orange), waiting for fixer (cyan), between iterations (purple), evaluating exit (yellow), or waiting for runner (yellow). The header shows a red Stop button and optionally a yellow Signal button when between-iterations mode is restart_on_signal. The iteration history table accumulates results as iterations complete.

transitions.name: Loop finishes all iterations or exit condition met (automatic)

states.name: Completed — Loop Finished Successfully
states.description: The loop has completed all iterations or the exit condition was met. The phase badge shows 'complete' in green. The progress bar is at 100% with green fill. The iteration history table shows all completed iteration results. The config form reappears, allowing the user to start a new loop.

transitions.name: User modifies form to prepare a new loop run
Start a new loop run after completion

states.name: Error — Loop Failed
states.description: The loop encountered an error. The phase badge shows 'error' in red. An error message appears in a red-bordered container with the error details. The config form reappears, allowing the user to correct settings and retry.

transitions.name: User modifies form to prepare a retry
Retry the loop after fixing configuration
